contexts.text: He shall be an onager man () = rational truth.

Of the same kind (as the horse, mule, and donkey) is the onager, for it is the mule of the wilderness, or onager; and it = the Rational of man not the Rational in its complex, but only rational truth. The Rational consists of good and truth... and it is rational truth that is signified by the onager. This, therefore, is what is represented by Ishmael.... It is the same thing whether you say rational truth, or the man whose Rational is of this kind. The man whose Rational is such that he is in truth only... is a morose man. (Continued. See Ishmael.)
A joy of wild-donkeys () = the devastation of intellectual things as to truth. ( = the love of falsities. AE 410:7.) AE 730:6.
It is said of the wild-donkeys that they snuff the wind () when inane and empty things are learned instead of real things, which are truths.
An onager alone by himself () = the Rational thus destitute of truths.
(Ephraim) shall be among his brethren as an onager ()... The Rational (of the Spiritual Church) is as an onager, the dissipation of which is treated of.
The wild-donkeys (which) quench their thirst () = the truths of reason. ( = the instruction of those in the Church who long for truths. AE 483:7.) AE 1100:9.

But truth separated from good, which is... here described... is like an onager; for it fights against all, and all against it; in fact it thinks of and breathes scarcely anything but combats; its general delectation or regnant affection is to conquer; and when it conquers it glories in the victory; and it is therefore described by the onager, or mule of the wilderness, that is, the onager which cannot be with others. Such a life is that of truth without good...

From scientifics and Knowledges alone, without a life of use, the Rational becomes... like an onager = morose, pugnacious, and possessed of a parched and dry life, from a certain love of truth, which (truth) is defiled with the love of self.
Wild-donkeys = those who are solely in rational truth.
There are beasts by which intellectual things, which are of truth, are signified... namely wild-donkeys, etc.
By the onager is signified truth separated from good.
His dwelling was with the wild-donkeys () = that the lot of his life was among the internals; for... wild-donkeys = those who are in direful falsities such as are in the Hells.
Is there not an infinite variety of men?... one like an untamed onager in front of a carriage...
